title: Full-history information used in paired and marginal-release analyses
note: *Note.* Both endpoints must describe the same known cohort, baseline and time scale, with one unweighted right-censored observation per patient and no delayed entry. Events take precedence over censoring at ties. Equal totals alone do not establish common membership. The risk convention is \(y(t)=\#\{X_i\ge t\}\). Complete tables require every exact event time and count, its pre-event risk, \(y(\tau)\) and all event history after \(\tau\). Statistical sufficiency does not establish permission to disclose or a privacy guarantee. A valid paired analysis is preferable when available. Administrative censoring preserves the upper endpoint using complete event-risk information through \(\tau\) and the exact horizon checkpoint (Section S4.5).

title: Simulation design and analysis availability
note: *Note.* All 39,000 planned samples were attempted. Support-valid samples include the two original computation failures; completed calculations exclude them. No unsupported or failed sample was replaced. The eight prespecified \(q>0\) core scenarios are a subset of the 12-scenario factorial family. Coverage among completed intervals and covered/planned yield have different denominators. The Supplementary Information reports the scenario definitions and targets. Data S1, sheets Method_summaries and Distribution_summaries, gives every method-specific summary.
